result.title: One-Way Coupling via Patchwise Adaptive Normalization in Transformer Surrogates
result.summary: Many physical systems exhibit one-way coupling: exogenous fields such as medium density or obstacle geometry influence the dynamics without being affected by them. We investigate how explicitly representing these fields can improve the accuracy and computational efficiency of transformer-based PDE surrogates. Building on spatially adaptive normalization, we introduce Patchwise Adaptive Normalization (PAdaNorm), which partitions exogenous fields into patches aligned with the state tokenization. We evaluate PAdaNorm on datasets from three different domains, using a Walrus-inspired transformer architecture. Across the three PDE families, PAdaNorm is on par with or up to 16% better than parameter-matched baselines in mean long-horizon variance-scaled RMSE on 60-step autoregressive rollouts. We also find that PAdaNorm better maintains hard physical constraints over long rollouts, such as preventing flow into impenetrable solid regions in porous media. When the conditioning is static, PAdaNorm caches the conditioning embeddings once and reuses them across the entire rollout, reducing inference FLOPs per step by up to 36% compared with parameter-matched baselines. An ablation over eight conditioning variants shows that modulating a single attention axis (temporal or spatial) suffices and that a lightweight shared MLP across blocks remains competitive with per-block projections.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究如何在 transformer PDE 代理模型中显式表示外生场（如介质密度、障碍几何），提出 Patchwise Adaptive Normalization（PAdaNorm），将外生场切块并与状态 token 对齐做归一化调制，在三个 PDE 数据集上评估长程自回归精度、硬物理约束维持与推理开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「切块与 token 化对齐的调制」及静态条件下缓存 conditioning embedding 的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据如何注入内部状态、以及深度/缓存对 latent 表示的影响提供可供核查的机制线索，但属远域迁移推测。
